newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- Prices mostly flat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- Prices mostly flat.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were mostly unchanged in light mid-Monday trade, while in new issues it was unclear whether a $920 million Port Authority of New York and New Jersey deal would arrive this week or next, market sources said.
"It hasn't been determined yet," a source familiar with the offering said. "It's up in the air. The papers on the transaction were just mailed."
On the secondary side, action was light.
"They are actually pretty flat, maybe slightly better in some spots because the market had a decent spin to it out of the chute," a municipal trader said. "But it's pretty quiet."
A trader of New Jersey paper said the market showed improvement late last week as retail buyers came in to take advantage of relatively cheap levels.
"We ran up quite a bit on Thursday and Friday, and I think we are just trying to digest these levels, just seeing what kind of interest we have."

Monday's actively quoted issues included Texas State Turnpike Authority Dallas North Tollway 5.0 percent bonds of January 2025. The bonds were bid at a 5.86 percent net yield, versus Friday's closing net bid of 5.85 percent.

Turning to new issues, this week's sales are expected to total $3.6 billion in 103 deals provided the Port Authority's deal via Lehman Brothers is included. The Authority's sale would be one of 38 negotiated sales totaling about $3 billion.
On the competitive side, 65 sales totaling $583 million are on the schedule this week. A $44 million Norfolk, Va., deal on Wednesday is the largest.
In debt futures, the June municipal contract was down 5/32 at 112-21/32. The June T-bond contract was down 6/32 at 107-26/32. The MOB spread was 155 ticks.

In the government cash market, the benchmark 30-year bond was down 8/32 at 94-14/32 to yield 7.07 percent. On Tuesday, the government is expected to sell $17 billion of two-year notes, followed by $12.5 billion of five-year notes on Wednesday.

The only economic data set for Monday is the March federal budget figure, due at 1400 EDT. Economists expect the deficit fell to $30.7 billion, from a $44.01 billion deficit in the prior report, according to a Reuters poll.
